correctness.rationale: In the ordered double boundary integral the four same-side terms sum to 2(a³+b³)/3, opposite sides give two terms of each orientation type, and the four adjacent pairs give eight copies of the corner integral. The opposite integral reduces to the one-dimensional triangular difference density 2(a−u); for the corner integral the divergence of (x,y)√(x²+y²) is 3√(x²+y²), giving the stated antiderivative formula from the top and right edges. Normalizing the two arclengths and then dividing by perimeter gives I/P³, not I/P². Differentiating gives 4(1+t)^4 R′(t)=F(t), F′(t)=2[(1+t)A−B+3(t−S)], and F″(t)=−2H(1/t), with H′(z)=(z−1)²(z+1)/(z²+1)^(3/2). As H(1)=3√2−3−asinh(1)>0 and F extends with zero at each endpoint, F is strictly positive inside. Near zero the dimensionless numerator is 4/3+4t+[1+2 log(2/t)]t²+O(t³ log(1/t)); dividing by 8(1+t)³ gives the claimed coefficient and constant. At t=1, F(1)=0 and F′(1)=−2H(1), giving R″(1)=−H(1)/32 and the stated Taylor law. This establishes the strict endpoint claims and equality conditions for all positive sides.
